scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, dimensions, construction, and performance testing guidelines for disposable (single-use) and reusable (multiple-use) dental bibs or napkins used during clinical and dental procedures to protect the patient, their clothing, and the surrounding medical environment from fluid transfer, water seepage, and microorganism transmission.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Medical Textiles / Personal Protective Equipment)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Medical Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all dental bibs or napkins manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 17354:2020 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified dental bibs in India is a punishable criminal offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Micro and small units are granted specific delayed implementation schedules, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to medical non-woven and cellulose paper bibs.

requirements.detail: Every commercial pack of dental bibs or napkins must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to verify compliance.

Dental bibs/napkins must be manufactured from suitable materials (typically absorbent cellulose paper or non-woven tops bonded with a leak-proof polyethylene film) that are not prohibited under any applicable laws or regulations. Consignment raw materials must be backed by the supplier's test certificate, and the manufacturer must declare that zero prohibited materials are used.
The standard covers disposable and reusable varieties. Size, shapes, and material compositions must be declared by the manufacturer for the scope of the licence.

The manufacture and preparation of the dental bibs/napkins must be conducted under proper hygienic conditions. The manufacturer must implement and record a systematic factory hygiene maintenance program.
Process controls must ensure the finished products are clean, flat, and completely free from lumping, holes, tears, or chemicals/substances that can cause tendering or degradation during storage.

The back layer must act as an effective barrier to liquid: when tested as per the waterproofness test of IS 14944, the backing must withstand standard water contact with zero seepage to protect the patient's clothing.
To maintain clinical hygiene, the total viable microbial count (bacterial and fungal bioburden) must be strictly controlled when evaluated in accordance with the standard methods of ISO 11737-1.

The bib must withstand mechanical handling and pulling. Both wet and dry tensile strength must satisfy specified minimum load thresholds (N Min) when tested in accordance with IS 15891 (Part 3) or IS 1969 (Part 1).

Under Amendment No. 1, the legacy 'Sinking time' absorption test is replaced with 'Liquid absorbency time'. The top sheet must absorb liquids rapidly when tested as per IS 15891 (Part 6) using the cylindrical wire basket method.

Under Amendment No. 1, the legacy 'water holding capacity' absorption test is replaced with 'Liquid absorptive capacity'. The absorbent layers must retain a high volume of fluid when tested per IS 15891 (Part 6) using the wire gauze support method. Note that absorbency tests are applicable to disposable dental bibs/napkins only.

Under Amendment No. 1, artificial saliva prepared in accordance with the chemical parameters of ISO 20701 is permitted as the test liquid for absorbency evaluations by mutual agreement between the buyer and the seller.

Each pack must be legibly and indelibly marked with: product name, size/dimensions, type (disposable/reusable), manufacturer details, batch/lot number, date of manufacture, and the newly mandated 'Declared shelf-life of the product' (inserted by Amendment No. 1).

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 17354 : 2020 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing disposable (single-use) and reusable (multiple-use) dental bibs or napkins used to protect patients' clothing and skin from saliva, water, and chemical splatters during dental and oral healthcare procedures. Under India's statutory Medical Textiles Quality Control Order (QCO), all dental bibs sold or imported domestically must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). The standard regulates key features—including a waterproof backing, high wet/dry tensile strength to prevent tearing, and restricted microbial bioburden to maintain clinical sterility. Amendment No. 1 (February 2024) updates the standard by introducing modern 'Liquid absorbency time' and 'Liquid absorptive capacity' parameters, allowing the use of artificial saliva (as per ISO 20701) for testing, and mandating that the product's shelf life be clearly declared on the packaging.
